gen-dafont-gobold-lora: Commanding and wide-set, Gobold stretches its big lowercase across the line, while Lora tightens things up with hairline curves and a welcoming c. Give the text serif a comfortable body size.
gen-dafont-gobold-noto-serif: Noto Serif takes the quiet side, with a prominent x-height and a subtle thick-and-thin rhythm. Gobold, the heading, holds its curve thickness firm and stretches out, which is the pair's sharpest edge.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-rowan: Groovy brings funky, loosely tracked lowercase with a c that nearly shuts. It does the playful shouting best, while Rowan, a text serif with generous curve openings and finer thin strokes, does the friendly reading.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-asap: Calm and stretched sideways, Helsinki looks drawn with a marker. It carries a single thread of reading best, whereas Asap, with open arcs and a low body height, handles the steady running text.
gen-dafont-helsinki-fs-quicksand: Clean and calm, Helsinki runs wide with a marker-drawn plainness and tall lowercase. And Quicksand echoes that build with glassy bowls and bars of identical thickness, so the two settle into each other on the page.
gen-dafont-helsinki-general-sans: Wide, marker-plain and tall in the lowercase, Helsinki sets a relaxed tone for General Sans to follow. And a body size a notch or two under the heading lets its x-height fill each line without crowding.
gen-dafont-hero-fs-asap: Asap reads in open arcs, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And if Hero is made small, its closed, bent-tubing letters lose that long sweep, while a large Asap would look oversized.
gen-dafont-hero-fs-epilogue: Contemporary and spaced out, Hero cuts its closed letters at a single depth. But shrink the heading and that sweep fades, while Epilogue's curvy, wire-like monoline lowercase would feel clumsy when made large.
gen-dafont-hero-general-sans: General Sans keeps its pen pressure steady from first letter to last. Hero is best at a long, slow sweep with closed shapes, while the body font does best at filling the line with smooth, open bends.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-epilogue: Big-bodied, curvy and unclamped, Klill and Epilogue share one monoline build. And over a long stretch, Epilogue's tall lowercase with stubby ascender tips keeps the plain sans text feeling approachable.
